title: Chaussons aux Pommes (French Apple Turnovers)
summary: Lightly spiced cooked apple sealed in puff-pastry half-moons, scored and baked until puffed and golden.
equipment: 12 cm round cutter or a small bowl

ingredients.item: Golden Delicious apples (about 3), peeled, cored and cut into 1 cm dice
ready-rolled all-butter puff pastry (2 sheets), chilled

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Cook the apples, sugar, butter, lemon juice and cinnamon in the saucepan over medium heat 8-10 min, stirring, until the apples are just tender; stir in the cornflour for 1 min until glossy, then spread on a plate and cool completely.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: On a lightly floured surface cut six 12 cm rounds from the pastry and roll each a little longer into an oval.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Spoon the cold filling onto one half of each oval, brush the edge with egg, fold over and press firmly to seal.

steps.title: Decorate
steps.text: Set on the lined tray seam-side down, brush with egg, score a curved leaf pattern with the knife tip without cutting through, and chill 15 min. Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Brush again with egg and bake 20-25 min until puffed and deep golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cool 10 min on the tray; the filling is very hot.

tips: Cool the filling fully or the pastry will go soft.
Seal the edges firmly so the filling stays inside.
Chilling before baking helps them keep their shape.
storage: Best on the day; keep 1 day in an airtight box and re-crisp at 180 °C for 5 min. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
